chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who remembers Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, among the oblivious ones is like the fighter among the battling ones.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a person who remembers God while others are heedless?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) draws an analogy between a person engaged in dhikr amidst the heedless and a warrior fighting among the enemy, highlighting the active, striving nature of remembrance in a state of spiritual neglect. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as dhikr being a form of *jihad al-nafs* (struggle against the self) and *jihad al-qalb* (struggle of the heart), where the individual stands firm in faith despite the surrounding cultural or spiritual apathy. This narration underscores the courage and vigilance required to maintain spiritual presence (*hudur*) when the majority is distracted by worldly concerns.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The Zakir (mentioner of Allahazwj) among the oblivious (unmindful) ones is like the fighter among the battling ones’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al- Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The speaker of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, among indifferent people is like a soldier on the offensive upon the enemies.”
